title: John chose to stay and serve until Christ returns
setting: In April 1829, Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery were translating the Book of Mormon at Harmony, Pennsylvania. They disagreed over whether the apostle John had died or remained on earth. John 21 raises the question but does not settle it. Joseph’s history says they agreed to ask through the Urim and Thummim. Joseph’s history calls it a translation of a parchment John wrote and hid. No account says Joseph had the parchment itself.
summary: The text is written in John’s own voice. The Lord asks John what he desires, and John asks for power over death to bring souls to Christ. The Lord promises that John will tarry until the Lord comes in glory. The Lord then explains to Peter why John will remain. Peter desired to come quickly to the Lord’s kingdom, and that was a good desire. John desired a greater work among men, so the Lord will make him “as flaming fire and a ministering angel” for the heirs of salvation. Peter will minister for John and James, and the three will hold the keys of this ministry. Both men receive what they desired.

contextNote.title: Why John did not die
contextNote.text: John 21 left readers unsure whether Jesus said John would not die. Verse 3 answers directly that John will “tarry until I come in my glory” and prophesy to nations. The reason is John’s own request in verse 2, for power over death to bring souls to Christ. Verses 4–5 contrast Peter, who wanted to come quickly to the Lord’s kingdom. The Lord calls Peter’s desire good and John’s a greater work. Verse 8 grants each man what he wanted. In this account, to “tarry” means to keep working among people, not merely to live long.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson pairs section 7 with the promise “even as you desire of me so it shall be” in section 6. What did John and Peter each desire in verses 2 and 4, and what does verse 8 say about both?
reviewNote: Read all 8 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, April 1829, Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery asking through the Urim and Thummim whether John was still living, and calls it a translation of John’s hidden parchment. JSP historical introduction read for the “difference of opinion,” John 21, and the note that no account says Joseph possessed the parchment. JSP says Revelation Book 1 places this after D&C 8; exact order of the April 1829 revelations is unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-12: setting credited the parchment description to the revelation itself; it comes from the heading/Joseph’s history. contextNote said the Lord calls both desires good; only Peter’s is called good (v. 5), John’s is a greater work.
